# Skills Reference — 54 Skills

Skills follow the open [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) standard and work in Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI and other compatible agents. Invoke them as `/name` where your workspace supports it, or describe the task and the agent picks the skill.

Install them with `./install.sh` (every detected workspace) or `./install.sh --target <workspace>`.

---

## Routing

### `/cofounder`
Your AI co-founder — thinks strategically, delegates to the right specialists, and gets it shipped

```
/cofounder <Describe what you need done>
```

### `/engineering`
Route any engineering task to the right specialist — backend, frontend, mobile, database, AI, DevOps, and more

```
/engineering <Describe the engineering task>
```

### `/product`
Route any product, design, or strategy task to the right specialist

```
/product <Describe the product or strategy task>
```

### `/business`
Route any business, operations, compliance, data, or content task to the right specialist

```
/business <Describe the business or operations task>
```

## Code Quality

### `/review`
Thorough code review covering logic, security, performance, and readability. For a fast security-only pass use /security-scan; for LLM-specific risks use /review-ai.

```
/review <File path or paste code to review (leave blank to review current file)>
```

### `/review-ai`
AI-specific code review — prompt injection, hallucination risks, token waste, eval gaps. For general code quality use /review.

```
/review-ai <File path, prompt text, or AI feature description to review>
```

### `/refactor`
Structured refactoring — improve code quality without changing behavior, with a safety checklist

```
/refactor <Paste code or describe what to refactor>
```

### `/debug`
Structured debugging — reproduce, isolate, hypothesize, fix

```
/debug <Describe the bug or paste the error message>
```

### `/security-scan`
Quick security scan of the current file or code — OWASP top 10, common vulnerabilities, fast triage. For a full code review use /review; for prompt injection and AI risks use /review-ai.

```
/security-scan <Paste code to scan or leave blank for current file>
```

### `/test-plan`
Generate a complete test plan — unit, integration, E2E, edge cases, and coverage targets

```
/test-plan <Describe the function, feature, or system to test>
```

### `/explain`
Explain any code, system, or concept in plain language — with analogies, diagrams, and examples. To produce lasting documentation, use /docs.

```
/explain <Paste code or describe what you want explained (leave blank to explain current file)>
```

```

```

## AI Startup Business

### `/pitch-deck`
Build or critique an AI startup pitch deck — slide-by-slide narrative, the metrics AI investors check, answers to "isn't this just a wrapper?", and a skeptical-investor teardown. Use when preparing to fundraise or reviewing an existing deck.

```
/pitch-deck <Describe the company and round, or paste/attach the current deck text and key metrics>
```

### `/investor-update`
Write a concise monthly or quarterly investor update for an AI startup — highlights, key metrics with trends, lowlights, AI cost and quality, hiring, and specific asks. Use when sending updates to investors, advisors, or your board.

```
/investor-update <Paste this period's numbers, wins, problems, and anything you need help with>
```

### `/pmf-check`
Assess product-market fit for an AI product — retention and usage signals, the "very disappointed" survey, customer interview evidence, AI-specific traps (novelty usage, demo-ware, wrapper risk), and what to do next. Use when deciding whether to scale go-to-market, pivot, or keep iterating.

```
/pmf-check <Share usage/retention data, customer feedback, survey results, or describe the product and traction>
```

### `/moat`
Assess and strengthen an AI startup's defensibility — wrapper risk, data flywheels, workflow depth, distribution, integrations, proprietary evals, and switching costs — and turn it into evidence for investors and roadmap priorities. Use when answering "what stops OpenAI/Google/an incumbent from doing this?".

```
/moat <Describe the product, customers, data you collect, and the competitors you worry about>
```

### `/ai-pricing`
Design pricing and packaging for an AI product — seat vs usage vs credits vs outcome-based models, plan tiers, free-tier limits, and gross margin after inference at different usage levels. Use when launching paid plans, changing pricing, or when heavy users are destroying margins.

```
/ai-pricing <Describe the product, customers, value delivered, current pricing (if any), and cost per task/request>
```

### `/security-questionnaire`
Answer enterprise security and AI-governance questionnaires for an AI startup — data handling, model providers and sub-processors, training on customer data, prompt injection, access control, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 status — and plan the controls needed to close enterprise deals. Use when a customer sends a security review, vendor assessment, or AI risk questionnaire.

```
/security-questionnaire <Paste the questions (or describe the customer), and describe your architecture, model providers, and current security controls>
```

### `/data-rights`
Assess whether an AI startup has the rights to use its data for training, fine-tuning, evaluation, retrieval and generation — customer data, scraped web data, licensed datasets, synthetic data from other models, user content and likenesses — and what permissions, contracts and policies are needed. Use before training on data, launching a feature that reuses customer content, or answering diligence questions.

```
/data-rights <Describe each data source, how you got it, and how you plan to use it (training, RAG, evals, outputs)>
```

## Docs & Community

### `/docs`
Write documentation for any function, module, API, or system. To explain code or a concept conversationally without producing docs, use /explain.

```
/docs <Paste code, function name, or describe what needs documenting>
```

### `/changelog`
Generate a CHANGELOG entry from recent git commits. For polished user-facing release notes use /release.

```
/changelog <Version number (e.g. 1.2.0) or leave blank to auto-detect>
```

### `/release`
Draft user-facing release notes — what's new, breaking changes, upgrade steps, migration guide. For a raw CHANGELOG entry use /changelog; for planning the rollout use /release-plan.

```
/release <Version number and optionally what changed (e.g. "2.0.0 — new auth system")>
```

### `/standup`
Generate a standup update from recent git activity and session context

```
/standup <Optional context — team name, any blockers, or what you're working on today>
```

### `/onboard`
Generate an onboarding guide for a new engineer joining this codebase

```
/onboard <Describe the project, stack, or specific area to onboard into (leave blank for full project)>
```

### `/devrel`
Build a developer relations strategy — community, DX audit, technical content, OSS, developer portal
